original_test_intent: Validate every applicable GPU device temperature sensor represented by TEMP_GPU 0~N, including identity, description, numeric reading and consistency across SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web against the approved GPU thermal specification.
original_method: The GPU thermal owner enumerates installed accelerators and identifies whether each temperature is die, board edge or another defined device sensor, maps it to a standard SDR or approved vendor query and Web row, and automation collects passive aligned evidence for every member.
manual_activity: The GPU/platform owner maps each installed GPU to its intended device-temperature sensor, defines sensor location and thermal limits, approves a standard or vendor-specific read method and confirms Web rows. GPU-memory temperatures remain outside this record.
required_inputs: Installed GPU count, slot/index, model, firmware and stable identity map
Exact 0~N applicability and distinction between die, board-edge, hotspot and memory temperatures
Per-GPU SDR record/entity or approved vendor query with netfn/cmd/data bytes and read-only provenance
Byte-level response decoding, units, signedness, scale, invalid/unavailable values and completion codes
Expected idle/load range, warning/critical thresholds, tolerance, freshness and ambient/load context
BMC/SDR/GPU firmware and driver versions plus BMC-Web mapping
Secret-safe access, complete evidence retention and no-clear policy
Thermal abort thresholds and independent console/cooling recovery
safety_requirements: Match this exact GPU device-temperature row; never substitute GPU-memory or adjacent UBB sensors
Enumerate every applicable installed GPU and explicitly record absent/not-applicable indices
Prefer documented standard read-only SDR access when it covers the target
Never guess or probe raw IPMI bytes; execute only an owner-approved read-only payload with known decoding
Do not create load, alter clocks/power/fans, flash/reset BMC or clear logs
Stop on invalid/stale/missing readings, rising thermal state, unexpected completion codes or BMC instability
Protect credentials and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify source identity, GPU inventory and temperature-sensor type
Collect complete standard SDR and Sensor List evidence before considering raw commands
Execute only a pinned owner-approved read-only vendor query and decode exactly as specified
Build per-GPU cross-view comparison and prepare Web rows for operator confirmation
Correlate passive GPU driver, thermal, fan, SEL and BMC health
Perform no guessed raw command, workload stimulus, control action or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve installed 0~N membership and device-temperature meaning
Approve the standard or vendor-specific query and byte decoding
Define thermal limits, load/ambient context, freshness and unavailable handling
Confirm each Web mapping and issue the final result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its refusal to invent a raw payload is correct, but the source does not prove that raw IPMI is mandatory; first determine whether complete standard SDR records expose TEMP_GPU. No command is executable until the mapping and expected decoding are approved.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Collect complete standard SDR/Sensor List inventories via secret-safe read-only access; if the approved GPU mapping is absent there, run only the pinned vendor read payload with documented completion codes and decoding, then reconcile every GPU with its exact Web row.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_GPU 0~N, BMC GUI, three-view criteria and 3/3-minute estimates are preserved; sensor count, raw bytes, decoding and thermal values are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES GPU SENSOR MAP AND APPROVED READ METHOD
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve installed GPU identity and sensor location first, test standard SDR coverage, then use a version-pinned read-only vendor payload only when necessary; align all readings by timestamp and thermal context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an unspecified assumption about raw IPMI with a documented standard-first decision path and exact byte-decoding gate.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One temperature per GPU may be die, edge or hotspot and cannot represent memory temperature; partial discovery or an undecoded byte is not three-view evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Passive reads are intended, yet unknown raw commands can be state-changing and an incorrectly decoded temperature can conceal a thermal fault.

project_override_considerations: GPU-less or partially populated builds require an approved applicability matrix. Platforms exposing GPU temperatures only through Redfish, NVML or a vendor daemon may use that documented read-only route if the source's SDR/Sensor/Web equivalence and identity mapping are explicitly approved.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and adjacent-sensor separation audit
Installed GPU index/slot/serial/model inventory and 0~N applicability
Per-GPU device-temperature location, stable sensor record and BMC-Web mapping
Approved standard or raw method with version, bytes, completion codes and decoding
Thermal specification with units, ranges, thresholds, tolerance, freshness and context
Complete redacted SDR/Sensor output and approved vendor output with status/timestamps
Per-GPU cross-view comparison plus GPU/fan/SEL/BMC health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets TEMP_GPU sensor information across three views. It omits topology, method and values but does not contradict the GPU-temperature identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive GPU-temperature evidence path is identifiable. The exact sensor map and query/decoding are supplyable platform inputs under ED-36; automation must remain gated until they are provided.

review_improvement: Preserves DeepSeek's safe no-guess boundary, tests standard SDR coverage before assuming raw IPMI, and prevents GPU-memory or adjacent UBB sensor evidence from satisfying the GPU device-temperature row.
independent_technical_reasoning: `TEMP_GPU` alone does not say whether the reported point is die, edge or hotspot, and a 0~N label does not establish installed membership. Raw IPMI is also not inherently read-only: safety depends on the exact net function, command and payload. The defensible path is topology-first, standard-inventory-first, and only then a pinned vendor read with explicit decoding and cross-view identity.
